title: Ignition Lockout (Alpine/MPO)
shortDescription: The Burnham Alpine or MPO ignition control failed to prove flame and locked out after retries.
fullDescription:
On Burnham Alpine condensing boilers and MPO oil-fired units the diagnostic LED flashes once per cycle to indicate ignition lockout. After three failed trials the control will not retry until the reset is pressed.

Causes range from a fouled spark electrode to a low gas-supply pressure event. Cracks in the porcelain insulator are a recurring problem on older Alpine V1 units.
safetyWarning: Gas appliance — if you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility emergency line.

fixSteps.title: Reset and observe
fixSteps.instruction: Press Reset; watch and listen for the ignition trial.

fixSteps.title: Clean electrode
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove and clean the spark/flame rod. Inspect porcelain for cracks.

whenToCallPro: Gas pressure verification needs a manometer and licensed gas tech.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep resetting?
faq.a: No — a few resets are fine, but unburned gas and lockout chasing should be left to a professional.

title: Pressure Switch Stuck Open
shortDescription: The vent/air pressure switch did not close at start of cycle.
fullDescription:
Two LED flashes on Alpine and ESC indicate the air-proving switch did not close. The control sees this as a blocked vent or a failed inducer.

Frozen condensate at the termination, a kinked vent hose, or a blower running below speed are typical culprits.
safetyWarning: Never bypass the pressure switch — that protection prevents CO spillage.

fixSteps.title: Inspect terminations
fixSteps.instruction: Clear snow, leaves, nests from intake/exhaust outlets.

fixSteps.title: Check hose
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the silicone tube off the switch and blow through it to confirm patency.

whenToCallPro: If the inducer or pressure switch needs replacement.

faq.q: Can I just bypass the switch?
faq.a: Absolutely not; you remove a code-required CO safety.

title: High Limit Open
fullDescription:
Three LED flashes mean the manual-reset high-limit tripped. On steam boilers (ESC, Independence) it usually accompanies a low-water condition; on hot-water units it points to circulator or zone-valve failure.

Before resetting, verify water level (steam) or pressure (hydronic) and that the pump is moving water.
safetyWarning: Investigate before pressing reset; repeated trips signal a real over-temp event.
symptoms: Boiler very hot to the touch

fixSteps.title: Let it cool
fixSteps.instruction: Allow the boiler to drop below 140 °F before resetting.

fixSteps.title: Inspect circulator
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the pump runs and the supply piping warms during a call.

whenToCallPro: Aquastat or circulator replacement is best left to a hydronic tech.

faq.q: Why does it trip after a power outage?
faq.a: Air enters the system and stalls the pump; bleed and refill.

title: Low Water Cutoff
shortDescription: LWCO has opened — water level is too low.
fullDescription:
Four flashes indicate the low-water cutoff is calling for water. On steam units this means the boiler needs water added or auto-feed is failing; on hot-water systems it means make-up pressure has been lost.

Do not bypass — running dry will warp or crack the cast-iron sections.
safetyWarning: Never short across the LWCO terminals; you remove a critical safety.

fixSteps.title: Top off water
fixSteps.instruction: Open the manual feed valve to bring level back to the normal mark, then close.

fixSteps.title: Hunt the leak
fixSteps.instruction: Check radiators, vents, and piping for staining.

whenToCallPro: If the LWCO needs replacement or the leak is hidden.

faq.q: How often should I flush the LWCO?
faq.a: Weekly during heating season for float-type LWCOs.

title: Flame Sensed Out of Sequence
shortDescription: Control sees flame when gas should be off.
fullDescription: Five flashes alert the operator that the flame-sense circuit reports flame outside the valid burn window. Treat as a possibly stuck gas valve or shorted flame rod.
safetyWarning: If gas odor is present, treat as a gas-leak emergency.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle the service switch and observe.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ignition assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Look for cracked porcelain, water staining, or shorted leads.

whenToCallPro: Suspected stuck gas valve must be diagnosed by a licensed gas tech.

faq.q: Can damp basement air cause this?
faq.a: Yes — moisture intrusion is a common Alpine issue near sump pumps.

title: Outdoor Sensor Open
shortDescription: Outdoor reset sensor is missing or failed.
fullDescription: When outdoor reset is enabled, the Alpine control monitors a 10K NTC mounted outdoors. Six flashes mean the sensor reads open or shorted; the boiler reverts to a fixed setpoint.
safetyWarning: No safety hazard — comfort impact only.
symptoms: Boiler runs at fixed high-limit setpoint

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Walk the run from outdoor sensor to boiler; look for breaks.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap with the OEM Burnham 102058-01 (or equivalent 10K NTC).

whenToCallPro: Only if you cannot reach the sensor location safely.

faq.a: Yes — the boiler defaults to fixed setpoint; bills may rise.

title: Supply Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Boiler supply NTC out of range.
fullDescription: Seven flashes indicate the supply temperature sensor (S1) is open or shorted. The control disables firing because it cannot enforce high-limit protection.
safetyWarning: Power off before disconnecting any sensor leads.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and replug the supply sensor at the board.

fixSteps.title: Replace if open
fixSteps.instruction: Ohm the sensor; replace if it does not read ~10kΩ at room temperature.

whenToCallPro: If the sensor well requires draining the boiler.

faq.a: No — always shut off power and let the boiler cool.

title: Return Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Return-water NTC sensor out of range.
fullDescription: The return sensor lets the control protect the heat exchanger from thermal shock and modulate firing. Eight flashes mean the sensor or harness is faulty.
safetyWarning: Disconnect line voltage before sensor work.

fixSteps.title: Reseat
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, reseat the return sensor harness.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: If still faulty, replace with the OEM sensor and refill the loop.

whenToCallPro: If draining and refilling is outside your comfort.

faq.q: Will the boiler run while it's faulted?
faq.a: No — return sensor is mandatory for safe operation.

title: Internal Control Error
shortDescription: Self-test on the ignition control failed.
fullDescription: Nine flashes is a generic internal-control failure. The board fails the boot self-check and refuses to operate. Surge events and water intrusion are common causes; sustained recurrence means replacement.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power at the breaker before opening the cabinet.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Off at the breaker for 2 minutes, then on.

fixSteps.title: Schedule replacement
fixSteps.instruction: If recurring, the board must be replaced and re-commissioned.

faq.a: Yes — adds years to control-board life.

title: Gas Valve Relay Fault
shortDescription: Control detected an internal gas-valve drive-circuit fault.
fullDescription:
Ten flashes indicates a gas-valve relay or driver circuit failure. The board cannot guarantee safe gas-valve closure and locks out.

Could be a shorted gas valve coil, a stuck relay, or a board-level FET failure.
safetyWarning: Treat as a serious safety event — call a professional and isolate the boiler gas supply.

fixSteps.title: Isolate gas
fixSteps.instruction: Close the manual gas shutoff at the boiler.

fixSteps.title: Call a tech
fixSteps.instruction: Schedule a licensed gas tech to diagnose with a meter.

whenToCallPro: Always — internal gas-valve drive faults are pro-only.

faq.q: Can I clear it and try again?
faq.a: Do not — this code suggests the boiler cannot safely shut gas off.

title: Air Pressure Switch Open
shortDescription: Air pressure switch did not close on a call for heat.
fullDescription: Burnham Alpine fault APS-OPEN indicates the combustion air pressure switch did not close after the inducer fan reached operating speed. Vent obstruction, condensate in tubes, or a failed switch are typical causes.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Drain APS Tubing
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the APS tube and drain.

whenToCallPro: Persistent APS faults need a technician with manometer.

faq.q: Why is this worse in winter?

title: Blocked Vent / Flue
fullDescription: Burnham Alpine BLOCKED-VENT fault is reported when sustained back-pressure indicates the flue is partially obstructed. Causes include nests, snow, ice, or excessive vent length.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.
whenToCallPro: If vent is clear, pressure switch testing is needed.

title: Flame Loss During Run
shortDescription: Flame signal lost while burner was firing.
fullDescription: Burnham Alpine FLAME-LOSS occurs when ignition succeeded but flame was lost during operation. Causes include weak gas pressure, air infiltration, or a contaminated flame rod.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.
whenToCallPro: Gas pressure verification is a technician task.

faq.a: Brief flame loss is contained — but persistent loss requires service.

title: Low Water Cutoff Tripped
shortDescription: Low water cutoff has detected insufficient system water.
fullDescription: LWCO-TRIP on Burnham Alpine indicates the boiler's water level safety has tripped. Causes include slow leaks, air binding, or expansion tank failure.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Refill
fixSteps.instruction: Open auto-fill valve to refill system per manual.

whenToCallPro: Persistent low water indicates a leak — call a plumber.

faq.a: Yes — but a sudden refill suggests a leak.

title: Gas Pressure Low
shortDescription: Inlet gas pressure below operating minimum.
fullDescription: Burnham Alpine GAS-PRESS fault indicates incoming gas pressure has dropped below the operating threshold. This may be a service-side issue, regulator problem, or oversized appliance load.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Test Other Appliances
fixSteps.instruction: Verify other gas appliances are operating normally.

whenToCallPro: Pressure testing is a technician task.

faq.a: Low pressure can cause incomplete combustion.
If multiple appliances are affected, yes.

title: Boiler Overheat
shortDescription: Supply temperature exceeded the safety high limit.
fullDescription: Burnham Alpine OVERHEAT fault indicates supply water exceeded the configured high-limit. Causes include circulator failure, closed zone valve, or scaled heat exchanger.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Verify Pump Running
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm circulator pump is energized when boiler fires.

whenToCallPro: Pump or zone valve replacement is a plumber task.

title: Sensor Out of Range
shortDescription: Supply, return, or DHW thermistor reads invalid.
fullDescription: Burnham Alpine BAD-THERMISTOR indicates one of the temperature sensors has failed open or short. Identify which sensor via the diagnostic menu.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Identify Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Use diagnostic menu to identify failed sensor.

faq.a: Different sensors can be similar but verify resistance curves.

title: Failed Ignition
fullDescription: FAILED-IGN on Burnham Alpine indicates the boiler attempted ignition the maximum number of times without flame. Causes include closed gas valve, weak igniter, or contaminated flame rod.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Clean Flame Rod
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and clean the flame rod.

whenToCallPro: Persistent failure needs technician with combustion analyzer.

title: Flame Rollout Detected
shortDescription: Rollout switch tripped, indicating flame outside the burner area.
fullDescription: ROLLOUT on Burnham Alpine indicates flame has been detected outside the combustion chamber — a serious safety event. Causes include blocked heat exchanger, vent restriction, or burner damage.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Shut Off and Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; inspect for visible damage.

whenToCallPro: Rollout requires immediate technician attention — do not reset and run.

title: Boiler Pump Fault
shortDescription: Internal circulator pump is not responding.
fullDescription: PUMP-FAULT on Burnham Alpine indicates the boiler's internal pump is not running or drawing abnormal current. Causes include air-locked pump, debris in impeller, or motor failure.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Bleed Air
fixSteps.instruction: Use bleeder screw on pump head to release air.

whenToCallPro: Pump replacement is a plumber task — partial drain required.

faq.q: Should I replace with same model?
faq.a: Match flow/head specs; check ECM compatibility.
